principles: Memory and playbooks are advisory context, never gate evidence
Prove the current failure before implementing the fix
Surface only active playbooks; candidates remain inert
Keep MVP1 session-scoped and defer broader consumers
drivers: The user wants hosts to stop relying on manual memory search
MVP1 must be observable through session_brief
Existing playbook lifecycle is candidate-only and must stay safe by default

options.name: A: Session-first advisory runtime pack
cons: Does not yet cover handoff/story/DONE consumers
Requires later MVPs for full runtime consumption

options.name: B: Implement all consumers before baseline
cons: Hard to verify root cause and output shape separately
Risks turning memory into pseudo-gate behavior too early

options.name: C: Build 1M baseline first
cons: Tests matcher/storage before real consumer wiring

rationale: Choose the session-first advisory runtime pack because it delivers the smallest observable improvement while preserving non-authoritative boundaries and leaving handoff/story/DONE plus 1M scale proof for later MVPs.

preMortem.scenario: Memory pack is mistaken for proof evidence
preMortem.consequence: Hosts may claim DONE or review assurance from memory
preMortem.mitigation: Hardcode gateEvidence:false and non_authoritative in pack/render text and tests

preMortem.scenario: Red test proves only candidate inertness, not runtime non-consumption
preMortem.consequence: Implementation may miss active playbook consumption gap
preMortem.mitigation: Seed an explicit active playbook fixture and assert session_brief currently misses it

preMortem.consequence: Session startup becomes noisy and unusable
preMortem.mitigation: Use maxLines <=60, top-N hits, omitted count, and focused smoke
